changes.before:
With $\chi_0\colon C(\Gamma_0)\to C(\Gamma_1)$ and
$\chi_1\colon C(\Gamma_1)\to C(\Gamma_0)$ as in
[[def-chi-zero-and-chi-one-wide-edge-morphisms]], assign to a crossing $p$ of a
tangle diagram the following two-term complex of matrix factorizations.

**Positive crossing.**
$$C_p=\bigl[0\to C(\Gamma_0)\{0,2\}\xrightarrow{\chi_0}C(\Gamma_1)\to0\bigr],$$
with $C(\Gamma_1)$ in cohomological degree $0$ (so $C(\Gamma_0)\{0,2\}$ sits in
degree $-1$); the shift $\{0,2\}$ makes the differential bidegree-preserving.

**Negative crossing.**
$$C_p=\bigl[0\to C(\Gamma_1)\{0,-2\}\xrightarrow{\chi_1}C(\Gamma_0)\{0,-2\}\to0\bigr],$$
with $C(\Gamma_1)\{0,-2\}$ in cohomological degree $0$ and
$C(\Gamma_0)\{0,-2\}$ in degree $1$; the overall shift $\{0,-2\}$ is the
normalization required by the Reidemeister IIa move.

In both cases the differential is $\chi_0$ or $\chi_1$ and has bidegree
$(0,0)$ as a map of the shifted terms.

**Recorded source conflict.** In the arXiv version (math/0505056v2) the prose
immediately before Figure 6 displays the negative crossing as
$0\to C(\Gamma_0)\{0,-2\}\xrightarrow{\chi_0}C(\Gamma_1)\{0,-2\}\to0$; this is
a typographical repetition of the positive display. Figure 6 itself, the
matrices (6), the degree typing, the IIa proof (section 5, where the standard
negative crossing complex is written
$0\to C(\Gamma_1)\xrightarrow{\chi_1}C(\Gamma_0)\to0$, see also the type IA
computation of section 4 and formula (10) of section 3) all force the
$\chi_1$-cone above; and the Euler-characteristic relation of section 7,
$\langle D\sigma_i^{-1}\rangle=q^{-2}(\langle De_i\rangle-\langle D\rangle)$,
holds for the $\chi_1$-cone with $C(\Gamma_1)$ in degree $0$ and would change
sign for the printed $\chi_0$ version. The published version of record
(Geom. Topol. 12 (2008) 1387-1425, formula (13), printed p. 1394) prints
exactly the $\chi_1$-cone.

Caveat: no absolute normalization is claimed; the $\{0,-2\}$ shift is fixed
only by the source's IIa normalization.
